answer: Agents earn reputation only through repeated trades settled from a bonded account: each new identity must lock scarce tokens, and counterparties release payment only after delivery is verified. A raven may spawn many accounts, but each needs its own bond and history; splitting one balance across them dilutes buying power and raises total capital at risk. At the nadir, a failed trade forfeits the bond, while a vertex of trusted agents can still discount proven peers, not newcomers.
